brief: carved pale-stone Veilfall falls-entrance arch/gate, about 6 m tall with an approximately 4.5 m clear opening, blue/teal Veilfall banners, wet dark rock plinths at its feet; open front +Z, base y=0, 20-30k tris
author: Claude (coordinator-side Tidewake Meshy art worker), owner-authorized Meshy use (Standing owner direction 1, 15 Oct 2026)
workflow: agent-drafted multi-view concept from repo references (Meshy image-to-image nano-banana-pro, references as data URIs) -> inspected -> Meshy multi-image-to-3d (latest, quad remesh, PBR textures embedded in GLB)
model_source_note: Model m_w01 was built from agent-edited views of concept c2: concepts/w_0.png is c2_0.png with its central arch section (x 150-455 of 608 px) stretched horizontally 1.75x in PIL (piers, banners and plinths untouched), then upscaled 2x; concepts/w_1.png is c2_2.png (side view) upscaled 2x. This was done because five nano-banana concepts would not draw an opening wider than about 2.8 m at 6 m height.
orientation: front (banners) faces local +Z, passage runs along Z, width along X, base at y=0, footprint centred on x/z

measurements.banner_side: +Z (banner geometry reaches z=+1.0, pier faces at about +-0.82)
measurements.method: gap in vertex x positions within a 12 cm horizontal band; mesh is open and see-through

native_size.note: Meshy raw GLB units, longest side ~1.9

scale_normalisation.method: lossless: GLB scene roots wrapped in node 'metres_root' with uniform scale + translation; base at y=0, footprint centred on x/z

previews: preview_3view.png (software flat-shaded 3-view, colours sampled per face)
files.raw_glb: not published (identical mesh to glb_metres minus the metres_root node)

concepts.prompt: A free-standing carved pale-stone ceremonial entrance gate for the Veilfall, the hidden stronghold behind the falls: two thick square stone piers joined by a wide, slightly pointed arch, like the falls-entrance arch on the attached board. Pale weathered limestone ashlar blocks with crisp carved mouldings, a layered arch frame with a carved keystone bearing a small white diamond emblem, a short carved cresting on top. On the front face of each pier hangs a long deep-blue and teal Veilfall banner from a dark iron bracket, with a white diamond-and-wave emblem and thin gold trim, swallowtail ends. At the foot of each pier sits a chunky wet dark basalt rock plinth, glossy and nearly black-blue, with small tufts of green moss and a few damp streaks running down the pale stone. The passage through the arch is fully open and see-through: no door, no wall behind, no waterfall. Real size about 6 m tall; the clear opening is about 4.5 m wide, so the arch is wide and generous; piers about 1.2 m square. Flat level base, the whole gate stands on one flat ground plane. Three-quarter front view. Stylised realism game asset in the Palworld/Animo style, chunky readable shapes, clean hand-painted PBR finish, same finish quality as the attached Tidewake driftwood arch. Absolutely no red, no oxblood, no crimson, no maroon, no pink anywhere. Single isolated object, full object visible, plain neutral light background, no scenery, no water, no text, no labels, no people, no creatures.

visual_verdict: Good: broad pale-limestone gateway with a stepped pointed-arch frame, pentagonal keystone with white diamond inlay, low cresting, square pier caps, two teal and deep-blue Veilfall banners on iron brackets on the +Z face, and chunky wet blue-black basalt plinths with moss and drip streaks at the pier feet. Normalised to 6.0 m tall: 9.49 m wide x 2.18 m deep, clear opening about 4.5-4.6 m up to 3 m, apex underside 4.07 m, 26,905 tris. Deviations: overall width 9.5 m is wider than a 6 m gate would usually be because the piers plus plinths are about 2.4 m each; the opening's apex is low (4.07 m), so the arch reads broad and squat; the keystone and cresting are horizontally stretched by the PIL widening (reads as a wide pentagon plaque); banner emblems are soft in the texture. Single material.
